title: Initial MS Procmon wiretap
description:
The wiretap reads the raw PML format (procmon.c) and passed the data to the Procmon dissector (packet-procmon.c) via WTAP_BLOCK_FT_SPECIFIC_EVENT.  The "dissector" treats the data more like a file, but it's the first step in integrating Procmon data into Stratoshark.

TODO: Add support for mapping numbers (process IDs, etc) to their respective metadata

Ping #20317

notes.body:
This is a VERY EARLY implementation of MS Procmon file support. I was able to copy/paste my way to cobble something together between https://github.com/eronnen/procmon-parser and pcapng-sysdig.c.  The file from #20317 can be read at the wiretap layer, but quickly crashes trying to be displayed at the "packet layer" because the "events" don't look like sysdig (no real surprise)
However, some architectural questions come out of this:
1. Currently Stratoshark is sharing wiretap library, however it really only needs the "read pcapng format" functionality out of it.  All of the other wiretaps are for Wireshark, so will we continue to have the wiretap library be a "superset" of file types supported by Stratoshark and Wireshark?
2. How should the procmon wiretap really be passing its data to the "dissector" layer?  Does it need its own WTAP_ enumeration value?  Should it use REC_TYPE_FT_SPECIFIC_EVENT? Do we start to break out Stratoshark dissectors into their own library or again are we going to make a superset?

Made more progress and starting using REC_TYPE_FT_SPECIFIC_EVENT.  Data from the wiretap is now passed up to a dissector that does some very basic dissection of the header and it treats the event data as raw bytes.
I guess Sysdig can still be used as an example to figure out how to populate the MS Procmon data into the "default" columns used by Stratoshark (MS Procmon data is pretty bare in terms of columns)
At this point it's really about porting more of the procmon-parser as it breaks down certain event data into more individual fields based on event type, etc.

@geraldcombs - I was able to dissect the "process" events and they have data that should be able to fill some of the Stratoshark columns, but I don't see how/where that's done.  Looking at packet-sysdig-event.c, I don't see all of the col_add_str() calls (or similar) that I would expect to have the columns populated. Where can I find information on how to "connect the dots" and have this be more of a Stratoshark dissector than a (packet) Wireshark dissector?

You might take a look at the Falco events plugin. In Stratoshark, packet-sysdig-event.c hands of dissection to the Falco events dissector if it's loaded, and the Falco events dissector uses libsinsp to fetch enriched syscall data.

Note that libsinsp currently only supports one pass for syscalls, and as a result we have to cache a bunch of field values.

...and to address your question about columns, you might want to add a "Process Monitor" profile in _resources/share/stratoshark/profiles_ similar to the CloudTrail profile. It has a set of column preferences and coloring rules that are suitable for CloudTrail logs along with an auto switch filter that switches to the CloudTrail profile if the capture contains CloudTrail data.

So all of the "data shown in Stratoshark" is not all natively in the scap file itself?  And "libsinsp API" is used to "fill in the gaps" (at the "dissector" layer)?
I haven't worked with profiles much to know how prevalent they are for the variety of protocols Wireshark supports, but this seems a little early to need a profile for the second filetype supported by Stratoshark?  I guess I thought I'd be able to find more "commonality" if it does make sense to have MS Procmon files part of Stratoshark.
Because I'm coming back to some of the same thoughts/discussions we had when ideas of Fileshark first started.  The "*shark engine" is (mostly) generic/powerful enough to parse out bytes in a buffer to turn into fields/columns, whether that's a packet or a fixed file structure.  It's the "additional analysis" that separates Wireshark/Stratoshark/Fileshark.  And I wanted to make sure that MS Procmon could take advantage of any "Stratoshark additional analysis".

So it appears that all Stratoshark hf fields are generated via create_source_hfids(), which uses the libsinsp API so the field names are effectively "hidden".  Is there any special about those field names that MS Procmon "dissector" should use, (i.e. proc.* or thread.*)?

> So all of the "data shown in Stratoshark" is not all natively in the scap file itself?

It's in the scap file, but the enriched data such as file descriptor to file path mappings are in metadata blocks. The Falco events dissector hands the processing of the metadata off to libsinsp. In theory we could parse the metadata blocks ourselves.

> I haven't worked with profiles much to know how prevalent they are for the variety of protocols Wireshark supports, but this seems a little early to need a profile for the second filetype supported by Stratoshark?

The default columns in Stratoshark use Falco events syscall fields (proc.name, proc.pid, fd.name, container.name, etc.). If the Procmon dissector has corresponding fields we could add them, but otherwise it probably makes more sense to add a separate profile.

> So it appears that all Stratoshark hf fields are generated via create_source_hfids(), which uses the libsinsp API so the field names are effectively "hidden". Is there any special about those field names that MS Procmon "dissector" should use, (i.e. proc.\* or thread.\*)?

They're dynamically generated inside a plugin, so you should check that they exist before trying to use them, but I don't see a problem with doing that otherwise.

Does the Procmon data expose PE file data anywhere? I ask because the Falco events dissector will call the ELF dissector if any I/O data contains an ELF header. I started on a PE file dissector a long time ago but never got around to finishing it.

Yes, the MS Procmon dissector could find the fields from inside the plugin, but what would happen if the plugin changed the field names?
I've been trying to think of analogies with Wireshark and the best I've come up with is if Wireshark had a OSI layer data model for its dissectors and several dissectors had to "share" network_layer.fieldX or transport_layer.fieldY.  Where would those fields live to be shared? Going off of field name prefixes from the falco plugin, there seems like there should be a "process dissector" (proc.*) and an "event dissector" (evt.*) independent of the plugin and that would be the "common" layer for Falco and Procmon to build off of (and any other file formats that have process or event information)

For the purpose of columns, we share fields via `packet_info`. That's easy in the network world because attributes like "source address" are baked in. It might be useful to come up with attributes that are generally useful in log messages, and add them to `packet_info` with associated column formats.
Should we start with the "default" columns of Falco events (or maybe the overlap of commonaility between Falco and Procmon)?
Maybe the commonality between Falco, Procmon, Kubernetes, and CloudTrail?
Sure, I'm just not sure what that is or how to get it.  It looks like Procmon is the only non-JSON, but as more "events based data" I assume we will find more commonality.

So I've ported as much as I can from https://github.com/eronnen/procmon-parser, but I feel like what I have right now is a "fissector" (half file dissector, half packet dissector).  However, none of it feels tied at all to Stratoshark "features" like event analysis and I'm not seeing how to do that.
The architecture of Stratoshark seems to run through the Falco event dissector (almost like it's the equivalent of the "frame" dissector in Wireshark), but Falco event dissector must have a strict "file format" that Procmon doesn't share.  Should Procmon "dissector" be ported to translate to that layer? (!21409 looks intriguing as an example of a "dissector" that adds to Stratoshark, but is already in Falco event format, because of the flexibility of JSON)

A lot of Stratoshark's focus on the Falco Events dissector comes from it being "first" and because that's what I've been working on in my day job. I don't think it's a big deal that Falco and Procmon have different file formats or that their respective file formats are tied closely to dissectors. I do think that having Procmon support is useful because it helps to identify things that we can generalize, such as the way events are routed from wiretap to epan or UI elements such a process table view.

I guess I was trying to determine if we wanted to address the "way events are routed" with this MR or if that's for a followup. I was treating "Procmon support" as being able to use the event statistics, etc that are currently in Stratoshark.
Should I just change this from a "fixes" to "ping"?  Procmon support seems "incomplete" with just the dissection.
